title: tapcheck.yml
description: What tapcheck needs to know about one web app. Only baseUrl is required. $NAME and ${NAME} (capitals) in any string are filled in from the environment when the file loads. Paths in gates, routes, flows and stub files are relative to this file's folder.

baseUrl.description: The http(s) address of the running app. A trailing slash is dropped.

app.description: How to start, stop and reset the app.

start.description: Shell command that starts the app. Skipped when the app already answers at `ready`; its whole process group is stopped after the run.

stop.description: Optional extra shell command run after the run.

reset.description: Shell command that puts the test data back. Runs first when RESET=1 (or when resetWhen says so); refused unless baseUrl is localhost, 127.0.0.1, *.localhost or *.test.

resetWhen.description: Globs on paths from the git root (the migrations and seed files, say). `reset` runs before a run when a matching file changed since the last reset, and on first use. Needs `reset`; ignored outside git.

ready.description: A path that answers once the app is up; any status under 500 counts.

allowRemoteReset.description: true lets RESET=1 run against an address that isn't local. Only for a remote throwaway copy.

audience.description: Who the app is for, in the words Jev is asked with ("a shop owner", "a nurse on a ward").

context.description: What kind of product it is and the conventions its users expect ("a dense, real-time trading tool; market terms and packed tables are intended"). Sent to Jev with every question.

expect.description: Findings that are right for this product: a fail or warn whose "<suite>: <check> @ <where>" matches `match` is recorded as info, saying `why`.

sides.description: Each kind of person who sees a different app, by name. Names are lowercase letters, digits and dashes, and can't be a suite or tag name.

baseUrl.description: This side's own address, when it differs from the top-level baseUrl.

csrf.description: This side's own CSRF probe, in place of security.csrf (another host often has other routes).

signedIn.description: A CSS selector on every signed-in page and not on the sign-in form (the account menu). A page without it means the session has ended, for apps that show their sign-in form at the same address.

screens.description: The pages a11y, audit and ux check and the crawl starts from: a list for every side, or a map of side name to list. With none, all four use /.

tasks.description: What a first-time user comes to do, for the usability suite: a list for every side, or a map of side name to list.

loginPaths.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) on a URL path. Being sent to a matching path means "not signed in".

skip.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) of links never followed. Setting it replaces the default.

interact.description: The interact suite: every safe control on the crawled screens is clicked, dialogs and tables are tried.

max.description: Most crawled screens clicked through per side.

submit.description: true also submits dialog forms the app itself must refuse or accept, with invalid and then valid input. That changes data: only for a throwaway database, as with app.reset; ignored unless the app is local or app.allowRemoteReset is set.

audit.description: The audit suite: the full UI audit of the screens.

max.description: Most crawled pages audited per side on top of the screens. 0: the screens only. Needs the crawl in the same run.

skip.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) of paths the audit leaves out, e.g. a canvas or an editor: /(editor|canvas)(/|$).

design.description: The design tokens. The audit lists computed styles that are not among them as warnings; a list left out isn't checked.

colors.description: Hex colours, in quotes: "#1f2937". Text, background and border colours are held to them.

fonts.description: Font family names; the first family of each text is held to them.

spacing.description: Paddings, vertical margins and gaps in px.

allowedHosts.description: Third-party hosts the pages may call; a request to any other is a failing finding.

publicWrites.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) of POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE routes that need no sign-in on purpose, e.g. ^/(login|webhooks/).

viewports.description: The screen sizes a11y and ux run on; the first is used by the crawl and flows, the first that isn't mobile by interact, audit and usability (audit adds a 768 px tablet and a 375 px phone of its own).

out.description: Where runs, signed-in sessions and state go. Git-ignore it.

budget.description: Most US dollars one run may spend on Jev. JEV_BUDGET overrides it.

headers.description: Extra headers sent with every Jev request.

keys.description: Shell command printing one translation key per line; ux then flags pages that show a raw key. Only dotted keys (orders.title) count.

changes.description: For CHANGED=1 and CHANGED=<git ref>: which files each part or suite depends on, as globs on paths from the git root. A part name (flow-checkout, a11y-customer) wins over its suite; "*" adds to every part; a part with no globs reruns on any change.

gates.description: Commands from the project's own toolchain, run as the part `code`. Exit 0 passes.

run.description: Shell command, run from this file's folder.

timeout.description: Seconds before the gate is stopped and fails.

warn.description: true makes a non-zero exit a warning instead of a failure.

routes.description: Shell command printing the app's routes as JSON: [{method, path, auth?}].

stub.description: A stand-in server for the outside services the app calls. Its address is TAPCHECK_STUB_URL.

rules.description: The first matching rule answers; anything unmatched gets 200 {}.

host.description: The outside host; also matches its subdomains.

path.description: A glob, or a regular expression when it starts with ^.

file.description: A file holding the answer, relative to this file's folder. It must exist.

not.description: A rule takes one of json, body or file.

dns.description: Also answer DNS questions over UDP, for an app that looks up domains. Its address is TAPCHECK_DNS (host:port). A name containing tapcheck-fail doesn't exist.

name.description: The full name asked for, such as shop.example.com.

values.description: A, AAAA: addresses. MX: a mail host, or "<priority> <host>". TXT: the text. CNAME, NS: a host name.

defaultA.description: The IPv4 address answered for an A question no record covers. Without it such a question gets no records.

coverage.description: COVERAGE=1: the coverage map merged from every run's hits.json.

file.description: Where the map is written, from this file's folder.

reasons.description: Gaps that are there on purpose: a route (as "GET /path") matching `match` is listed with `why` instead of GAP.

parallel.description: How many flows of a side run at once (PARALLEL=<n> overrides it). A flow with serial: true runs alone; the suites run one by one either way. The app must handle that many users at once.

flows.description: Globs of flow files (TypeScript or JavaScript); each file is its own part, flow-<name>. Flows may change data.

marks.description: Marked screenshots (MARK=1 or MARK=0 overrides it for one run): a failing or warning finding's evidence opens with the screen as it was measured, a banner saying the check, and a box, a number and a note on each element the check knows (audit, a11y, crawl, interact, and t.mark in flows). What Jev judged gets the banner alone.

mailpit.description: The address of Mailpit's web page, for t.mail in flows.

args.description: Extra command-line switches for the run's Chromium, e.g. --disable-features=LocalNetworkAccessChecks for an app on localhost whose sandboxed frames load its own files.

csrf.description: A request sent without a token on each side that signs in (every side when none does); it must be refused with exactly `expect`.

expect.description: The HTTP status the app answers with, e.g. 403 or 419.

login.description: How this side signs in. Leaving it out means none.

oneOf.description: none: no sign-in. manual: a visible browser opens /login and a person signs in once.

manual.description: The sign-in page a person signs in on, in a visible browser. The session is kept until it expires or LOGIN=1.

command.description: Shell command printing a Playwright storageState JSON: {"cookies": [...], "origins": []}.

fields.description: Field to value. A key is a CSS selector, else a name attribute, else the label's text. Use $NAME for secrets.

submit.description: CSS selector of the submit control. Default: the first submit button.

totp.description: Filled in when the app asks for a one-time code.

screen.description: A page by `path`, or by `from` + `link`: the first link on the `from` page whose path matches.

path.description: A path on the side's baseUrl, or a full URL.

link.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) tested against each link's path.

suffix.description: Added to the matched link's path, e.g. /edit.

purpose.description: What the screen is for; the five-second test needs it.

goal.description: What the person is trying to do.

done.description: The screen that means the goal is reached.

notDone.description: What the screen shows when it isn't.

optimal.description: The fewest clicks that reach the goal.

text.description: What the person would type into a search field on the way.
